Polynomial joint trajectories

Source: R/trajectories.R
robot_traj_polynomial.Rd

Cubic polynomials match endpoint positions and velocities; quintic polynomials also match endpoint accelerations. Each joint gets its own polynomial on \([0, T]\); outside this interval the trajectory is held at rest at its endpoint positions. The boundary conditions are satisfied exactly.

Usage

robot_traj_polynomial(
  q0,
  q1,
  duration,
  times = NULL,
  n = 101,
  qd0 = NULL,
  qd1 = NULL,
  qdd0 = NULL,
  qdd1 = NULL,
  order = c("quintic", "cubic")
)

Arguments

q0, q1

Start and end configurations.

duration

Duration \(T\) in seconds.

times

Optional sample times; otherwise n equally spaced samples.

n

Number of samples.

qd0, qd1, qdd0, qdd1

Endpoint velocities and accelerations (zero by default). Accelerations are ignored by cubic trajectories.

order

"quintic" or "cubic".

Value

A robot_trajectory whose evaluate(t) function returns positions, velocities and accelerations at arbitrary times.

Examples

tr <- robot_traj_polynomial(c(0, 0), c(1, -1), duration = 2, n = 5)
tr$q
#>           [,1]       [,2]
#> [1,] 0.0000000  0.0000000
#> [2,] 0.1035156 -0.1035156
#> [3,] 0.5000000 -0.5000000
#> [4,] 0.8964844 -0.8964844
#> [5,] 1.0000000 -1.0000000
